inline_comments.comment: This file should not be committed. It is a personal development scratch page named after the contributor. Per project conventions, development scratch files must not be checked in — use `demos/dev/` for ephemeral demos, and any committed demo under `demos/` must be registered in `demos/index.html`. Additionally, the diagram inside uses `"dogs" : -60.67`, which will now throw a validation error under the new `addSection` guard, making this file non-functional even as an informal test.
Typo in `accTitle`: `"simple pie char demo"` should be `"simple pie chart demo"`.

This line silently drops valid user data: `.filter((d) => (d.value / sum) * 100 >= 1)` removes any section whose value is less than 1% of the total, with no warning or error. This is an undocumented, breaking behaviour change for users with legitimate small-percentage slices (e.g., `"Rare event" : 0.3` in a chart totalling 100). The stated goal of this PR is to reject negative/zero values — those are already handled by `addSection` throwing. There is no justification given for silently discarding valid positive data. At minimum: (1) log a `log.warn` with the filtered label and value, (2) document this threshold in the pie-chart docs, or (3) remove the filter entirely since D3's pie layout handles small-but-positive arcs without crashing.

`sum` is computed twice from the same `sections` map: once inside `createPieArcs` (line ~13 of the new code) and again here with `sections.forEach(...)`. Both computations produce identical results. The one inside `createPieArcs` can be removed; pass `sum` from `draw` into `createPieArcs` as a parameter, or just compute it once at the top of `draw`.

`filteredArcs` is dead code. `createPieArcs` already removes every section where `(value/sum)*100 < 1`. Any datum remaining in `arcs` therefore satisfies `(value/sum)*100 >= 1`, which means `((value/sum)*100).toFixed(0)` will always be `'1'` or higher — never `'0'`. The filter `arcs.filter((datum) => ... !== '0')` is always a no-op and `filteredArcs` always equals `arcs`. Remove it and use `arcs` directly in the two `.data()` calls below.

Both new tests use `.rejects.toThrowError()` without asserting on the error message. Per project rules, when a crash is converted to an explicit `throw new Error(...)`, tests should verify the specific error is thrown — not just that *any* error occurs. Consider using `.rejects.toThrow('Zero and negative values are not allowed')` (or a regex matching the key phrase) to pin the contract and prevent silent regressions where a different, unrelated error masks a missing validation.

The test title `'should render pie slices only for non-zero values but shows all legends'` is misleading: all three values (386, 85, 1) are already non-zero. What this test actually exercises is the new < 1% filter — `"Rats": 1` is approximately 0.21% of the total 472 and would be dropped from the pie arcs while still appearing in the legend. The title should reflect the actual behaviour being tested (e.g., `'should omit slices below 1% of total from the pie but include them in the legend'`).
Double space before `INT_PIE`: `FLOAT_PIE |  INT_PIE` — should be a single space for consistency with other grammar files in the project.
File is missing a trailing newline. All text files should end with a newline character.

Per project changeset conventions, the description body should begin with a conventional commit type prefix followed by a space and a capitalised description — e.g., `fix: Add validation for negative values in pie charts`. The current entry has no prefix.

`"Prevents crashes during parsing by validating values post-parsing"` contradicts itself in a single sentence. The validation is in `addSection`, which runs during DB population (after the Langium parse step). Either say "Prevents crashes by validating values during DB population" or "Prevents crashes at parse time" — not both.

general_comments.comment: The PR bundles two unrelated concerns into one change: (1) **validation** — throwing an error for zero/negative values in `addSection` (the stated bug fix); and (2) **silent filtering** — removing sections below 1% of total from the rendered pie slices (an undocumented new behaviour added in `createPieArcs` and `pieRenderer`). These should be separate PRs. Mixing them means the silent filter ships without review discussion, documentation, or an explicit decision. It also makes the changeset description inaccurate, since the 1% filter is a visible rendering change that affects existing valid diagrams.

There is no Cypress end-to-end test covering the actual validation path — i.e., a diagram with a negative or zero value resulting in a rendered error state (or no render). The new `cypress/integration/rendering/pie.spec.ts` snapshot test exercises only the happy-path rendering with all-positive values. An e2e test that passes a diagram with a zero or negative value and asserts the expected error output would close this coverage gap and prevent future regressions.
